messages:
anna: Heads-up — Windows devs hit a weird auth collision today. I have a Credential Manager entry (redwood) that our helper reads, and the sample-app .env has REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY checked in. The SDK ended up sending both which triggered a `conflicting_auth` 401 mid-stream and the chat restarted. Anyone familiar with Credential Manager interactions?

nadeem: Ugh. Windows cred helpers are a special case. Can you paste the outbound headers (sanitized)?

anna: From our staging proxy logs (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer credmgr_ephem_123",
  "X-Redwood-Project": "proj_dev_abc",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
Response: 401 {"error":"conflicting_auth","detail":"multiple auth mechanisms present"}
```

yasmin: That matches the pattern we've seen elsewhere but with a different source (cred manager). Two quick asks: 1) SDK should never emit two auth headers; pick one deterministically and drop the rest. 2) developer UX: provide an `auth inspect` CLI that shows which source would win without sending requests. Example: `redwood auth inspect --path .` -> prints `resolved: Authorization from credential-manager (priority: 40)`.

anna: Love `redwood auth inspect`. Would have saved me 20m. Also on Windows the credential helper is often installed by other tooling so it's easy to be surprised.

nadeem: For precedence proposal (my take): explicit param > CLI flag > credential-helper > env (REDWOOD_ORG_KEY then REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY unless REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true) > netrc > legacy. Rationale: credential managers are more explicit than checked-in .env but less explicit than CLI flag.

yasmin: I worry about CI: if org key is injected into CI env, a checked-in project .env could override unexpectedly. Default rule should keep CI stable: env injected by CI (ORG) should beat checked-in project env. Ok to have credential-manager between CLI and env, but document defaults clearly. Also a `--auth-source` flag is necessary for CI pinning.

rust-sdk-bot: note: Rust SDK maintainers request a machine-checkable conformance test. Suggest adding `tests/devex/auth_precedence.yml` that runs across node/python/rust matrices and verifies header emission for given env/netrc/credhelper combos. Will add ticket: DEVEX-8001.

yasmin: Also: streaming recovery. When we get a 401 mid-stream because of rotation/expired token, SDK should attempt an in-flight refresh via an onAuthRefresh hook before tearing down. If the hook returns a new token, swap headers and resume. Only escalate if refresh fails.

anna: Concerning logs: please ensure tokens are masked in any diagnostic output; but include `X-Auth-Source: credential-manager` (no secret) behind a `REDWOOD_DEV_HEADERS=true` toggle. That makes ops debugging possible without leaking secrets.

nadeem: Good point. Implementation checklist I propose:
- Add AuthResolver module with canonical precedence and a public table in docs
- Implement `redwood auth inspect` CLI command (dry-run resolution)
- Emit a WARN at startup if >1 auth source detected; rate-limit to once/minute per process. Message example: `WARN devex auth: multiple auth sources detected; using credential-manager. Run 'redwood auth inspect' or pass --auth-source to override. https://redwood.dev/auth`
- Do not send multiple auth headers; enforce single header in all SDKs
- Add onAuthRefresh hook for streaming transports and implement in SDKs (Node/Python/Rust)
- Add conformance tests across SDKs and include the Rust matrix (DEVEX-8001)
- Add optional dev header `X-Auth-Resolved` when REDWOOD_DEV_HEADERS=true (value: credential-manager|env|netrc|...).

yasmin: Extra DX idea: an `auth-lint` pre-commit hook that scans for checked-in .env files containing REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY or REDWOOD_ORG_KEY and warns or fails in repos that opt in. That would prevent accidental commits of project keys to sample-apps.

anna: I can open the sample-app PR to remove checked-in .env and add .env.example. I'll include instructions for Windows devs about the credential manager and `redwood auth inspect` once implemented.

qa-bot: ticket created: DEVEX-8001 "Auth precedence conformance + auth-inspect CLI"; assigning to @rust-sdk, @node-sdk, @python-sdk.

yasmin: One more rotation edge-case: credential-manager entries can be stale after rotation. On receiving 401/403 and if the winning source was credential-manager or netrc, invalidate and re-resolve once before failing (and surface an actionable message like "credential-manager token invalid; run 'redwood auth login' or set --auth-source").

nadeem: Agree. Also ensure the warning is helpful and not too noisy; rate-limit and include a link to troubleshooting.

anna: Thanks all  I'll open the PRs and the RFC for `redwood auth inspect`. cc @dev-tools and @security.
